articles.title: President Zelenskyy condemns Russian drone strike as 'atrocity'
articles.description: A Russian drone strike on a passenger bus in southern Ukraine has killed five people and wounded at least seven. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy calls the attack an “atrocity” and part of ongoing strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure. The attack happened Wednesday in the Nikopol district near the war's front line. Zelenskyy also reports a passenger train was struck in the Mykolaiv region, but passengers were evacuated. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha says over 500 locomotives have been damaged since the war began. Ukraine is urgently seeking replacements. Meanwhile, Zelenskyy denies claims of a truce on energy infrastructure attacks.

Gaza building collapse kills at least 19 people
articles.description: A building housing displaced Palestinian families has collapsed in Gaza City, killing at least 19 people, most of them women and children. The structure was heavily damaged during the Israel-Hamas war and there had been warnings about its safety. Dozens of people remain missing or trapped under the rubble following the collapse on Wednesday. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia said its air defenses intercepted a drone headed toward Mecca late Tuesday. The kingdom's military spokesperson emphasized the security of the holy city as a “red line.” The Houthis have denied targeting Mecca, but the allegation drew widespread condemnation.

articles.title: ‘We are prey’: discovery of seven women’s bodies fuels anger over femicide in South Africa
articles.description: String of female murder victims found near Johannesburg’s international airport, including five in the past week The discovery of the bodies of seven women around Johannesburg’s international airport, including five in the past week, has prompted an outpouring of fear, grief and anger over a lack of progress in tackling femicide. When Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo did not return after going for a run on 9 September, her eight-year-old daughter alerted relatives, who contacted police. The 38-year-old’s body was found on Saturday and identified by relatives on Monday. The news of her disappearance had gone viral. Continue reading...

articles.title: Iranian football returns in the shadow of war and with row over last league title
articles.description: Prolonged league suspension due to war and falling behind Saudi spending power are weakening the sport in Iran Just three months ago, Iran was one of the biggest stories in football as Team Melli arrived at the World Cup to try to play in the US, a country that had been bombing and firing missiles at Tehran and other targets. A disallowed goal and a last-minute effort that hit the bar in the final group game against Egypt confirmed Iran’s group-stage exit – to the delight of some US officials – by the narrowest of margins. It also signalled the abrupt end of international attention. This week there was a return, however, to international action as Esteghlal and Tractor SC started out in the AFC Champions League Elite. It comes after the Persian Gulf League kicked off in mid-August, almost six months after it was postponed at the end of February, and subsequently abandoned as the war continued. Continue reading...

articles.title: San Francisco's 'rideshare rapist' sentenced to 150 years in prison - Tue, 15 Sep 2026 PST
articles.description: When rideshare apps were still in their relative infancy, Orlando Vilchez Lazo was driving around San Francisco posing as a driver to pick up women coming out of bars and nightclubs. He'd get them in the car and drive them to secluded locations and sexually assault them, and repeated the act numerous times for years. His first attack was in 2013, but in 2018, one of his victims escaped, and Lazo was taken into custody.
